requirements.note: Three-column grid of 600 HSL tiles with emoji centred, newest first, filling the width inside 16pt margins; heart badges on liked tiles.
Pull-down menu with All boards plus ten boards and a checkmark; Coast shows 64 tiles; menu is also on the Liked screen.
Push to a large view with board, title and 'Added <date>'; a paging collection view where the next tile follows the finger and peeks in; prev/next chevrons and 'n of 600'.
Full-width Like/Liked button in the large view; the Liked tab shows the same grid (63 after one like) with its own filter.
Select → circle overlays, count in header, Select-all, floating Like/Delete bar; bulk Like becomes Unlike when everything selected is liked; Delete asks to confirm and removed 2 tiles (600→598).
Bulk likes and the 2 deletions were still there after relaunch.

bugs: The delete confirmation pops up as a popover at the top of the screen, with its arrow pointing at the filter button instead of the Delete button the user tapped.
tells: Heavily themed look (cream background, rust accent, serif detail title, letter-spaced eyebrow text 'A LITTLE DAILY INSPIRATION', decorative layers/heart icon badge): more of a branded marketing feel than a stock iOS app.
Large view's nav title is a generic 'Inspiration' rather than the tile's name; the '1 of 600' row stays pinned and content scrolls under it with no material at large text.
Select mode's floating Like/Delete bar is hand-drawn pills rather than a bottom toolbar; at the largest text it covers all but one row of the grid and repeats '1 selected' twice.
The Select All control is an icon-only checkmark circle in the leading nav slot, which isn't a standard place for it.
A.scroll: Native-feeling: the large title collapses into an inline bar with blur, flings decelerate smoothly with no blank or popping rows, and scroll position is kept on returning from a tile.

requirements.note: Edge-to-edge three-column grid with 2pt gutters (Photos-style), newest first, 600 tiles; heart badges on liked tiles.
System pull-down menu from a blue 'All Boards ⌃⌄' button, ten boards plus All; Coast shows 64 tiles. The chosen filter is kept across relaunch.

Large view shows title, board and date, and swiping left/right does change tile. But it isn't a real pager: mid-swipe only the emoji slides inside a static coloured square and the next tile never peeks in, so it feels like a gesture recogniser rather than paging. Needs a 'Swipe the tile to explore' hint.
Heart button in the nav bar toggles like/unlike; Liked tab shows the same grid (63) with its own filter.
Select → circle checkmarks, 'n selected', Select All, icon-only heart/trash buttons; Delete shows a centred alert with Cancel/Delete and removed 2 tiles (600→598).
Likes and deletions were still there after relaunch.

bugs: At the largest text size the floating tab bar covers the prev/next/position row of the large view until you scroll.
In select mode the bulk Like button stays an outline 'like' heart even when every selected tile is already liked; there is no Unlike state.
tells: Swipe between tiles doesn't track the finger as a paging scroll view would: the colour square stays put and only the symbol moves.

The filter/count header is pinned above an inner scrolling grid. Content never scrolls under the nav bar, the title is inline-only (no large title), and at the largest text the pinned header eats about a quarter of the screen.
The accessibility tree wraps the whole app in an extra ScrollView/'app' container with stray horizontal scroll bars, a sign of a non-native view hierarchy (seen only in tree, not felt).
A 'Swipe the tile to explore' instruction label, which is unusual on iOS.
In select mode the Like/Delete buttons are hand-drawn icon-only grey pills rather than a bottom toolbar.
B.scroll: Flings and deceleration feel normal, with no blank rows, and position is kept on returning from a tile. But the grid scrolls inside a fixed header box rather than under the nav bar, so it lacks the collapsing-title, under-bar-blur feel.

why: Both apps meet every requirement and persist correctly. A's large view is a true paging browser where neighbouring tiles follow the finger, and its large title collapses natively as the grid scrolls under the bar. A's bulk Like also switches to Unlike sensibly. B is plainer and closer to stock in places (system alert, Photos-like grid), but its tile swipe doesn't track the finger, its header is pinned over an inner scroll view, and its tab bar covers the detail controls at large text.
